rows: Yellow fever is a mosquito-borne viral infection.
Risk occurs in specified parts of Africa and the Americas.
Vaccination is the principal preventive measure for eligible travellers.
Country entry requirements may require an International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis.
Pre-travel assessment should consider destination, itinerary and individual contraindications.
Mosquito-bite avoidance remains important after vaccination.
Suspected illness after travel requires urgent clinical assessment.
Current country and outbreak information should guide advice.
Travel to a risk country or a vaccination certificate does not establish infection or complete protection.
Conclusions require itinerary, timing, vaccination, contraindications, mosquito exposure, symptoms, laboratory and current guidance.
Japanese encephalitis is transmitted by mosquitoes in parts of Asia and the Western Pacific.
Most infections are asymptomatic, but encephalitis can be severe.
Travel risk depends on destination, season, duration and activities.
Vaccination is recommended for selected travellers at increased risk.
Mosquito-bite prevention is required whether or not vaccination is given.
The vaccine schedule should be completed in time for exposure where possible.
Individual contraindications and precautions should be assessed.
Suspected neurological illness after travel requires specialist evaluation.
Travel to Asia or vaccination status does not establish an individual's infection risk.
Conclusions require exact itinerary, season, rural exposure, duration, vaccine course, mosquito precautions and clinical evidence.
Tick-borne encephalitis is a viral infection transmitted mainly by infected ticks.
Risk occurs in defined endemic areas of Europe and Asia.
Outdoor activity and season influence exposure risk.
Vaccination is available for travellers and workers at increased risk.
Protective clothing, repellents and tick checks reduce exposure.
Unpasteurised dairy products can be a transmission route in some settings.
Neurological illness after relevant exposure requires urgent assessment.
Diagnosis uses clinical, exposure and laboratory evidence.
A tick bite or travel to an endemic country does not establish tick-borne encephalitis.
Conclusions require location, season, activity, tick or food exposure, vaccination, symptoms and laboratory evidence.
Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease is a rare progressive neurodegenerative prion disease.
Different forms of CJD have distinct epidemiological and clinical features.
Suspected cases require specialist neurological assessment.
Diagnostic evaluation uses clinical, imaging, cerebrospinal-fluid and other specialist evidence.
Cases are monitored through national surveillance.
Infection-control precautions are required for specified tissues and procedures.
Instrument management depends on tissue infectivity and patient risk category.
Public-health and specialist advice should guide unusual exposure incidents.
Rapid cognitive decline or a screening result does not establish CJD.
Conclusions require clinical course, specialist tests, imaging, tissue or procedure exposure, classification and expert evidence.
